kitDescription: Maxwell is an Iron SR Attacker whose Skill 1 fires every time the team enters Full Burst: the two allies with the highest final ATK (herself included, since nothing excludes her) gain Charge Speed +4.48% and ATK +43.1% for 10 seconds. Her Skill 2 would give her Critical Rate +4.83% and Critical Damage +13.91%, but only when more than five enemies are on the field, so it never activates in a single-boss solo raid. Her burst swaps her rifle for a piercing railgun; measured fight footage shows this resolves as one heavy railgun shot per cast at 813.42% of final ATK, rather than a sustained multi-shot weapon swap. Because the cast lands before the Full Burst window opens, the shot does not receive the +50% Full Burst bonus. Most of her damage still comes from her charged sniper normal attacks, with the railgun shot a minor addition.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHA found. Skill 1 (all four lines) converges across driver, S2b, S5, and S6 — including the subtle byFinalAtk/self-eligible targeting, which was the driver's one genuine encoding fix this gauntlet — and the driver's M1–M4 tests each discriminate against their named nearest-wrong (burstCast keying, allies:all scope, wrong magnitude/duration). Skill 2 is a correctly documented inert slot: all four agents independently rejected the ungated-crit-passive misread, the line is verbatim in unmodeled, and S5 proves the inertness assertion is non-vacuous. The burst is the one cross-family divergence, and it is measurement-gated by design: the probe (run G) established the single-shot railgun topology by falsifying the kit-literal weaponSwap at 1.93 hot, the driver ships exactly the prose's own 813.42% number through the correct burst-cast routing (crit-eligible, core-ineligible, noFb), and the collapsed swap scaffolding is verbatim in unmodeled with a ⚑ recipe — so every S5 red assertion is a RECON_ERROR-side artifact of the blind agents deriving the unfalsified text hypothesis, not a driver defect; notably S6's own caveat anticipates the single-shot outcome. The residual the owner should spot-check is the magnitude instability honestly flagged in kit-status (0.80 on run G vs 1.17 on N6, 'audit candidate') — including whether the real railgun shot cores (kitParse F2 notes flatDamage strips the core the Pierce railgun may roll), which could explain part of the run-G under-read; that is a measurement question for the N6/G re-audit, not an encoding fix, and must not be 'solved' by refitting numbers to the board. Same-model residual: all agents share the fullBurstEnter-vs-burstCast and top-2-vs-all priors, so convergence there proves stability, not correctness — but those two points are exactly what the driver's discriminating counterfactuals pin behaviorally.
